items.title: Quest Log
items.text:
• Princess Knife and his crew are looking for mercenaries to assist their expedition into Castle Xyntillan
  • The High Priest of the Temple of the Three Testaments has gone missing in Castle Xyntillan
  • Blerot the Woodsman has gone missing in Castle Xyntillan

items.title: The Three Testaments
items.text: The Symbol of the Three Testaments

items.title: Overview
items.text:
The Three Testaments is the most commonly-worshipped god in Chamrousse. As an abstract deity, it is depicted as either three separate gods (known as The Triplets) or as three aspects of the same god (known as The Trinity). Tripletism is official representation recognized by the Temple of the Three Testaments in Chamrousse, though the local priests will welcome any variation of the faithful.

The Three Testaments are a manifestation of three core concepts that guide its faithful:

  1. "Exalt Thyself"
  2. "Exalt Thy Neighbor"
  3. "Exalt Thy Village"

The exact meaning of the Testaments, their order, and relative importance have led to multiple schisms and civil wars between the faithful throughout history. As a general rule, however, civilized settlements welcome adherents to the Testaments, as they tend to make good citizens in polite society.

items.title: The Xyntillan Family
items.text: The original builders and current owners of Castle Xyntillan. Rumored to be using dark magic of some kind to preserve their immortality. Besides Jean-Giscard, no Xyntillan family member has been seen outside the Castle in years.

items.title: The Black Comedian
items.text: A tavern with a small theater stage and a connected boarding house. The tavern's name comes from an actor who reportedly died during a performance many years ago.

items.title: People
items.text:
• Fernand Bonnel owns the establishment and lives upstairs
  • Etienne acts as the tavern's security and occassional server during busy hours

items.title: Notes
items.text:
• Fernand offers The Special - a handwritten note with a rumor about Castle Xyntillan or Chamrousse - for 5 coins. A disclaimer on each rumor protects Fernand from legal liability, should the rumor prove false.
  • Fernand was using cut-rate flour to produce the tavern's infamously stale bread. Chef has taken over bread baking duties, much to Etienne's relief.

items.title: Castle Xyntillan
items.text:
A day's travel North of Chamrousse, the road passing through the mountains branches. The well-traveled path leads to the rest of the Northern Reaches, but the path less-traveled leads through a mountain valley. On the shores of a crystal-clear lake found here, one may find the crumbling parapets and fantastic towers of Castle Xyntillan.

Castle Xyntillan's exterior, showing the gatehouse to the courtyard and main entrance

items.title: History
items.text:
The PCs have begun stitching together pieces of the Castle's history. What they already know is:

  • The Castle has stood for hundreds of years
  • It was originally the seat of power in the region before the current monarchy absorbed Chamrousse and the nearby villages
  • It was (and still technically is) owned by the Xyntillans, who are rumored to be immortal
  • Somewhere within the Castle lies a hoard (or hoards) of priceless treasures that the Xyntillans have "acquired" over the centuries.

items.title: The Blind Beast of Xyntillan
items.text: According to a witness in The Tap, the Blind Beast of Xyntillan is a massive eyeless ape with the face and tail of a crocodile.

items.title: Jean-Giscard Xyntillan
items.text: The youngest Count of the Xyntillan family. Jean-Giscard lives with his wife and children in self-imposed exile in a town called Tourssevoy, a four-day journey from Chamrousse. He was sent away from his family at a young age to be raised and educated in the North, and wants nothing to do with his eccentric family and their legacy.

items.title: Etienne
items.text: A quiet ex-mercenary captain that currently acts as the bouncer at The Black Comedian. He is well-known by the mercenaries at The Tap.

items.title: Details
items.text: Human male, mid-forties. Scar running down the left side of his face.

items.title: Fernand Bonnel
items.text: Owner of The Black Comedian. Also owns the attached boarding house and the town's boat launch.

items.title: Details
items.text: Human male, short and greying with a handsome face. Not a great baker and self-conscious about it. In a personal and professional rivalry with Pascal Levesque.

items.title: Report
items.text:
The session began on clear spring night in Chamrousse, the 15th of Highspring. The player characters (PCs) found themselves listening to performances of Elvish poetry in The Black Comedian until they were interrupted by the arrival of a local man named William, who collapsed on the floor of the tavern with an arrow stuck in his back.

Alara and Antoine carried the wounded man to the town infirmary where they met Madame Geraldina, the town healer. Geraldina tells the good samaritans that many adventurers have met similar fates in the nearby Castle Xyntillan. Antoine recovered a scroll from William before learning he died from his wounds the next morning.

The PCs, now intrigued, decided to team up in order to learn more about the Castle. Probing the locals, they discovered that the Castle was once the seat of political power in Chamrousse. The Xyntillan family has since gone missing amidst rumors that they cling to immortality inside the walls of their home with some kind of powerful magic. Travelers of all kinds now flock to Chamrousse, seeking the family's alleged hoard of priceless treasures held deep within Castle Xyntillan's walls.

During their investigations, the characters encountered a number of colorful characters in Chamrousse:

  • Fernand Bonnel, owner of The Black Comedian, its attached boarding house, and the local boat launch.
  • Etienne, a former mercenary with ties to The Tap who now guards The Black Comedian.
  • Jacques Valt, bristly owner of The Chimera Apothecary.
  • Madame Geraldina, the town healer, located at the infirmary attached to the Temple of the Three Testaments.
  • Princess Knife, whose adventuring party also seek the Castle's hoard.
  • Pascal Levesque, owner of the rough-and-tumble mercenary bar on the town's outskirts simply called The Tap.
  • Count Jean-Giscard Xyntillan, the youngest Count of the Xyntillan family, living in self-imposed exile in the nearby town of Tourssevoy to avoid his family.

By paying Fernand for The Special, the party also revealed the following local rumors (which may or may not be true, warned Fernand!):

  1. There's another Xyntillan named Jean. He is not the same man as Jean-Giscard Xyntillan. Do not get them mixed up, as it will anger both of them.
  2. The Royal Tax Collectors would pay a reward for physical evidence that the Xyntillan hoard is real (implicating them in property tax avoidance).
  3. Blerot the Woodsman swore to avenge his murdered lover, but disappeared in the Castle without a trace just a few months ago.
  4. An old chimneysweep has told lurid tales of concealed shafts and secret doors in the fireplaces. A little soot won't hurt you!

Finally, the players discovered the following pieces of information about the Castle itself:

  • A mercenary in The Tap told a tale of the Blind Beast of Xyntillan, a monstrous, eyeless ape with the face and tail of a crocodile. It hides amongst the statues in the Castle's courtyards, pretending to be one.
  • Those who attempt to climb the courtyard walls are assaulted by large, violent ravens.
  • Shadowy figures stalk intruders from atop the Castle's walls.
  • Those who have infiltrated the Castle's lakeside balcony entrance returned mad, repeating tales of "talking faces" that haunted them.
  • Besides Blerot, the town's previous High Priest of the Three Testaments has also gone missing in Castle Xyntillan recently.
